rules.rule: [any] Message templates are compile-time constants with named PascalCase placeholders, one argument each, and escaped braces; no Serilog {@X}/{$X}. Checked by CA2254, CA2253, CA2017, CA2023 and CA1727 at error, plus an rg for the operators.

[any] Every log call in src is a [LoggerMessage] partial method, and hand-written LoggerMessage.Define is not used (DefineScope excepted). CA1848 and CA1873 are errors. The test layer sets both to none, and brownfield code follows a ratchet.

[any] Every generator parameter appears in its template; a state-only parameter needs a reasoned SYSLIB1015 pragma. SYSLIB1015, 1013, 1002, 1012, 1018 and 1025 are errors, and so are LOGGEN000 and LOGGEN002 when Telemetry is referenced.

[any] Each [LoggerMessage] has an explicit EventId that is unique across the assembly, and shipped method names are frozen. Needs SYSLIB1006=error (it is Info and per-class) plus a reflection uniqueness test.
[any] Compute an expensive argument inside an IsEnabled guard, into a local, and call a SkipEnabledCheck=true method; do not guard cheap arguments. CA1873 is an error.
[any] Pass the exception object as the Exception argument, never ex.Message, ex.ToString() or {Ex}. Checked by an rg plus SYSLIB1013 and CA2017.
[any] Log a failure once, where it is handled; no log-and-rethrow. A library never logs Error for a failure it throws or returns. Checked by a multiline rg.
[any] Follow the level table: in a library, Information is for rare lifecycle events only, per-operation detail is Debug or Trace, and Critical is never used.
[any] A scope uses key-value state or DefineScope, is wrapped in using, is opened once per operation and holds no secret. An rg catches BeginScope($"...") and discarded scopes.

[any] No secret reaches a log record, and payload logging is opt-in and allow-listed. Cites CS-PROC-08, CS-API-06 and CS-ERR-08. Checked by a FakeLogger canary across Message, State, Scopes and Exception.
[any, apps] An app that logs regulated data classifies it and calls EnableRedaction. Production console logging uses JSON or SingleLine. A library never references the redaction packages.
[any] Assert logs with FakeLogger<T>, never a mocked ILogger.

[lib] Choose the channel by shape. A one-choke-point library takes no logging or telemetry package and uses the in-box ActivitySource/Meter plus data or a callback. A long-lived, many-class client takes MEL.Abstractions only. Checked with a nuspec grep after pack.
[lib w/ MEL] Reference the lowest Abstractions version that compiles (8.0.x on the net8 floor) and use static this-ILogger generator methods. Apps pin 10.x.
[lib w/ MEL] The entry point takes ILoggerFactory? = null, normalised to NullLoggerFactory.Instance. DI-built types take a non-null ILogger<T>. No LoggerFactory.Create and no static logger in src.
[lib] No ad-hoc diagnostics: RS0030 bans T:System.Console, T:System.Diagnostics.Trace and Debug.Write*.
[lib] Exactly one static readonly ActivitySource and one Meter, named after the package id, with public const names and a version with +sha stripped. The corrected rg also catches target-typed new().
[lib] Start the Activity with using var inside the async method that awaits the work, never in a sync Task wrapper. A test asserts Activity.Current is unchanged afterwards.
[lib] Make every tag, status and metric write null-safe with ?. or an IsAllDataRequested block; compute no tag value before the null check.

[lib] Tags come from a closed, checked-in allow-list. Never record argv, executable path, env, cwd, streams, resource names, Exception.Message or stacks. No AddException, and no stream lines as events.

[lib] On failure, set Error with a fixed-template description and error.type = the exception type's full name, the same on span and metric. Success and caller cancellation leave status Unset. Never set Ok.
[lib] One Histogram<double> in seconds named <lib>.client.operation.duration, with at most 2 bounded tags, recorded under .Enabled.
[lib] While net8.0 is a TFM, no .NET 9+ telemetry API is called unconditionally (AddException, InstrumentAdvice, ActivitySource(name,version,tags)).
[lib] Span tests use an ActivityListener with both ShouldListenTo and Sample, filtered by the test's own TraceId.

[ocx] OcxTelemetry exposes SourceName and MeterName = Ocx.Sdk. One span per call, named 'ocx {command}', kind Client. Exactly 5 tags (process.executable.name, process.exit.code, error.type, ocx.command, ocx.attempts). Metric ocx.client.operation.duration tagged ocx.command and error.type. The README documents AddSource, AddMeter and the ILogger bridge.

[ocx] Every call sends --log-level <level> appended to the CS-PROC-07 prefix and before the verb. The level comes from a closed OcxLogLevel enum, default Warn, through an explicit switch. Trace and Debug are documented as possibly exposing secrets. src never sets OCX_LOG_LEVEL, OCX_LOG or RUST_LOG.

[ocx] Stderr is data first (redacted, capped Stderr and StderrTruncated; StderrExcerpt on exceptions). The live stream is one client-level Action<string>? OnStderrLine: lines redacted before the call, delivered in pump order, nothing after return, and no IProgress<T>. Stderr never reaches telemetry or classification.

[ocx] Guard each OnStderrLine call. Capture the first fault with ExceptionDispatchInfo, stop calling, keep draining, and after ocx exits rethrow that exception unchanged from the awaited call. This is the one added CA1031 site under CS-ERR-06.
[ocx] Do not inject, forward or scrub TRACEPARENT, TRACESTATE or BAGGAGE; ocx reads none. Revisit when ocx does.

conflicts_resolved: Library dependency: logging-rules said a library depends on MEL.Abstractions, while library-instrumentation said the SDK takes no logging package. Decided by library shape: one-choke-point wrappers take none (in-box DiagnosticSource; NU1605 measured; 0/9 wrappers use ILogger); long-lived many-class clients may take Abstractions only.

Abstractions version: logging-rules said pin 10.x everywhere; instrumentation said use the lowest. Apps pin 10.x. A packable library references the lowest version that compiles (8.0.x) and uses static extension methods. The 8.0 generator rejects the primary-constructor form on net8.0 and net10.0 with SYSLIB1019 (lib-floor fixture, watched).

Throwing stderr callback: instrumentation swallowed the fault and disabled the callback. Decided: guard, stop calling, keep draining, rethrow after exit. Watched red-swallow and green-rethrow; MEL itself surfaces provider exceptions as AggregateException (mel-throw); the Python house rules block silent swallows. This adds one site to CS-ERR-06.
Callback type: csharp-async allowed IProgress<string> or Action<string>. Decided Action<string>: Progress<T> delivered 5436 of 50000 lines out of order (cb red-progress).

--log-level position: instrumentation put it first, while CS-PROC-07 fixes the prefix as --format json --color never. Decided to append it after the prefix and before the verb. Watched on ocx 0.6.5: 0 stderr lines with off, 6 without the flag, exit 64 after the verb.

Status description: semconv says use the exception message, and instrumentation's reason against it (Message carries argv) is stale since CS-ERR-08. A fixed template is kept anyway: an rg cannot tell OcxException from a BCL exception, the launch message names the exe path, and semconv says SHOULD, not MUST.
Log-level default: Python sends --log-level only when configured; C# always sends it, default warn, because ambient RUST_LOG/OCX_LOG=trace floods stderr and 0.6.5 ignores OCX_LOG_LEVEL.
Per-attempt ocx.attempt vs per-call: decided one span per public call with an ocx.attempts count, so span and histogram share a unit.
Static-source rg: instrumentation's pattern missed target-typed new(...), catching 1 of 3 planted constructions; the corrected pattern caught 3 of 3, watched.

Level policy: the brief said 'libraries never log Information', but exemplars contradict it. The rule is narrowed to Information for rare lifecycle events only. Azure's 'log thrown exceptions at Warning' is rejected in favour of logging once at the handler.
another_round: csharp-observability-library-instrumentation cross-OS: do the CS-OBS-27/28 callback order, deferred rethrow and no-call-after-return guarantees hold on Windows (host SDK 10.0.102) and arm64, and does the TraceId filter isolate spans under xUnit v3 parallel runs? All callback fixtures used POSIX sh on Linux x64.

ocx contract tier, trace secrets: does ocx 0.6.5 or main print OCX_AUTH_* values, bearer tokens or Authorization headers at --log-level trace during an authenticated pull or push? The offline probe found none. If they appear, Trace needs redactor hardening, not just a doc warning.
csharp-async callbacks and streaming: Action<string> is settled. Is a later IAsyncEnumerable<string> stderr stream worth its back-pressure and cancellation semantics?
owner_decisions: CS-BUILD-24 and CS-JSON-14 disagree. CS-BUILD-24 says the nuspec has 0 dependencies, but CS-JSON-14 puts System.Text.Json 10.0.12 in the net8.0 group (measured: 1 dependency). Recommend amending CS-BUILD-24 to allow exactly System.Text.Json on net8.0.
Should the ocx CLI read TRACEPARENT (OTel env-carrier, Release Candidate)? If yes, CS-OBS-29 flips to injecting from Activity.Current. Until then the SDK neither injects nor scrubs.
The package id (open CS-API question 2, default Ocx.Sdk) becomes the permanent telemetry SourceName and MeterName const.

rules.rule: Keep the security analyzer category at All in every project, src and tests. A project that lowers AnalysisLevel sets AnalysisModeSecurity=All. Add no per-rule severity line for a security ID and never lower one.
Ship the 40-line BannedSymbols.Security.txt and set RS0030 and RS0031 to error in .globalconfig. The union of all BannedSymbols*.txt files must contain no duplicate symbol.
Give every Regex a match timeout of at most 1 s. Patterns are constants or Regex.Escape output. A library never sets REGEX_DEFAULT_MATCH_TIMEOUT.

Never let wire data name a type, assembly or code path. Unions decode only through the CS-JSON-07 tag-first converter; no JsonDerivedType, Type.GetType, Activator.CreateInstance(string,string) or Assembly.Load*.

Do not add System.Xml parsing, XSLT, System.Data, P/Invoke, BinaryFormatter, Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration or SecureString to src. If XML is unavoidable, use only XmlReader.Create with DtdProcessing.Prohibit and a null resolver.
Never suppress a security diagnostic in src (CA2100/2119/2153, CA2300-2369, CA3xxx, CA5xxx, SYSLIB0011/0060, RS0030/0031). In tests, only CA5394 with a reason.
Draw every random value in src from RandomNumberGenerator, retry jitter included. Guid.NewGuid is an identifier, never a secret.
Authenticate downloaded bytes in one helper (SHA-256, FromHexString, FixedTimeEquals) shared by archive, pin and sidecar. Ocx-reported OCI digests stay ordinal string identifiers.
Keep the packed nuspec budget: the net10.0 group is empty and net8.0 holds System.Text.Json only. Gate on the nuspec, never on dotnet package list.

Declare build-only packages (analyzers, MinVer) as GlobalPackageReference, or PackageReference with PrivateAssets=all. Never put asset metadata on a PackageVersion. Run the evaluated-item gate per TFM.

List every package whose build, analyzer or tools assets run in the build in eng/build-code-packages.txt. Triage a candidate's content before its first build. Use ExcludeAssets for packages you do not trust.
Every new package ID passes the nuget.org existence and owner check (NOT-FOUND blocks), and the PR body answers the six-question review.
Packed-closure and build-code packages carry an allow-set licence expression (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3-Clause, ISC, 0BSD) or a recorded human decision.
Use Dependabot only, with nuget and dotnet-sdk ecosystems, cooldown of at least 3 days, groups, and a reason on every ignore entry.

Keep signatureValidationMode at accept at v1 and never set DOTNET_NUGET_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION=false. Generate any later require config with dotnet nuget trust source, and never claim it is enforced on macOS.
No SBOM in the nupkg or on PRs. If one is requested, attach CycloneDX -ed output to the release.

(Models b and c) Commit ocx-pins.json with 8 SHA-256 values for TestedOcxVersion. In model c, compile it into OcxPins; a manifest row that disagrees fails before any archive request, and the archive must equal the pin.
Regenerate pins only through triangulation: the dist.json row, the release sha256.sum and the GitHub asset digest must agree. Never take a digest from a single source.
(Model c) A version other than TestedOcxVersion needs a caller-supplied digest or an explicitly named TrustManifestOrigin option, never a default.
Keep Ed25519, minisign, NaCl, BouncyCastle and Sigstore code and packages out of the core assembly at v1.
Library code never spawns gh, cosign, minisign or openssl, never passes --no-verify, and never sets OCX_NO_VERIFY.
Verification fails hard: no warn tier, no skip, disable or allow-unsigned option, and no environment switch.
The README and the entry point's XML docs state what the pin proves, what it does not, and that a located binary is not verified.
(Model b) Before dotnet pack, check every staged runtimes/*/native/ocx* against ocx-pins.json.

(Dormant until ocx publishes a P-256 signature) Verify dist.json.sig with ECDsa P-256/SHA-256 in Rfc3279Der format, with an SPKI constant held in the assembly, a curve assert, at most two keys selected by key ID, no network, and fail closed. A Sigstore add-on pins the exact SAN and binds the subject digest itself.

conflicts_resolved: Polymorphism: UNSAFE's [JsonDerivedType] allow-list, which throws on unknown tags, loses to CS-JSON-07/CS-API-08's tag-first converter with an Unknown arm. Both stop wire data from naming a type; only the converter stays forward-compatible.

FixedTimeEquals everywhere (UNSAFE N11) vs CS-JSON-15 string digests: FixedTimeEquals applies only to authenticating downloaded bytes, through one helper. Ocx-reported OCI digests stay ordinal string identifiers.
CA5394 pragma for jitter (UNSAFE) vs no security suppression in src: jitter uses RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32, so src needs no CA5394 suppression.

RS0030 severity line (UNSAFE) vs 'TWAE already makes it an error' (CS-BUILD-13): the line is added. Measured: with -p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=false, 24 RS0030 became warnings and the build exited 0; with the line it exited 1.

Ban fragment merge: duplicate symbols across BannedSymbols*.txt raise RS0031, an error under TWAE. Measured with a duplicate DangerousAcceptAnyServerCertificateValidator line. The existing posture fragments already collide on 9 symbols (CS-BUILD-15 vs CS-PROC and CS-XP-11, CS-BIN vs CS-XP-10 and packaging banparams, CS-BIN-16 vs this fragment). Each symbol now lives in one owner file, and CS-BUILD-15's 5-line starter is superseded.

Dependency budget: CS-BUILD-24 says 'none on net8+', but CS-JSON-14 puts STJ 10 on net8, measured as 1 direct and 2 transitive packages. The budget is net10 = 0 and net8 = System.Text.Json only, gated on the nuspec.

MinVer: CS-PKG-06's PackageReference with Version= breaks CS-BUILD-23 (NU1008 under CPM). It becomes a GlobalPackageReference, which was measured never to reach the nuspec. SUPPLY's 'everything as GPR' and CS-PKG's 'PrivateAssets=all' are both accepted, and the evaluation gate is the check.

NuGet require mode, owners and the nuget verify sweep (SUPPLY R6-R8): not adopted at v1. They do not stop typosquats and are inert on macOS, and CS-BUILD-27's empty packages folder plus default Linux and Windows restore verification cover the cache-poisoning case.
Historical hazards (BinaryFormatter family, XXE defaults, entity bombs) are table rows, not rules. The BinaryFormatter and NetDataContractSerializer ban lines are dropped unless an ns2.0 slice ships.
ATTEST proposed 16 CS-BIN rows (20-35). They are merged to 9 (CS-BIN-20..28): 20+21 merged, 27+28 merged, and 24/25/26/29/32/33 folded into one dormant v1.x rule.

rules.rule: Set Nullable=enable only in the root Directory.Build.props. Write no #nullable directive (enable, disable or restore) in any hand-written .cs file under src or tests.
Never promote or suppress nullable warnings by list. No WarningsAsErrors of 'nullable' or CS8xxx, because TWAE already covers them. No 'nullable', CS8xxx or CS9264 in NoWarn.

Allow '!' in src only in two forms: '= null!;' on a [JsonRequired] member, or with a same-line '// null-forgiving: <invariant>' comment. Never write 'default!'. Set IDE0370 to error in .editorconfig, with EnforceCodeStyleInBuild on.

Annotate every public Try* out parameter: [NotNullWhen(true)] out X? for non-generic methods, [MaybeNullWhen(false)] out T for generic ones. Put [DoesNotReturn] on throw helpers, [MemberNotNull] on init helpers and [NotNullIfNotNull] on pass-through returns. Never return an unconstrained T? to signal a miss.

Guard every reference parameter of a public or protected member of a public type with the throw helpers on its first lines. Never write new ArgumentNullException(. Set CA1062 to warning for src, reversing CS-BUILD-12's none. In async methods the guard faults the returned Task.
Test for null with 'is null' / 'is not null', never '== null' / '!= null'. Parenthesize 'not' when it is mixed with 'and' or 'or'.

Treat a '?' change on a shipped public signature as contract. Review it in the PublicAPI.Unshipped diff and list it in the release notes. RS0016 and RS0017 are the only gate; package validation does not see these changes.

Never call .Reverse() on an array. Call Array.Reverse or Enumerable.Reverse explicitly, and ban MemoryExtensions.Reverse<T>(Span<T>) with RS0030. Under LangVersion 14 the same source reverses in place on net8.0 and is a no-op on net10.0.
Test projects inherit the src TFM list, and every behavioural test runs on every TFM.

Keep Span<T> and ReadOnlySpan<T> out of public signatures, and never mix span, array and IEnumerable overloads. Use Span and stackalloc only in synchronous internal helpers, outside loops. Never use unsafe or AllowUnsafeBlocks.

Name no identifier 'field' (nor union, closed or extension), and never '@field'. Give every non-nullable field-backed property an initializer or 'required'. Never write 'field ??=' on state that two threads can touch; use Lazy<T> instead.

Public extension blocks contain methods only. Extension properties, static members and operators are internal. A static BCL polyfill block is internal, has the BCL's semantics, and is commented with the TFM that has the real member.
Declare no user-defined compound assignment operators (void operator +=) and no instance increment or decrement operators.
Use a?.B = c only where a null receiver is a legitimate state, never to silence a nullable warning.

Ship no preview switch: no EnablePreviewFeatures, no updated-memory-safety-rules Features, and no -p:LangVersion or -p:EnablePreviewFeatures in workflows. Fix CS8652 or CS9327 by deleting the syntax, never by changing LangVersion.
Write no #if NET11_0_OR_GREATER region while TargetFrameworks has no net11.0. Such a region is never compiled and rots.

Once an SDK 11 GA pin adds net11.0, use per-TFM LangVersion (15 on net11.0 only). Put C# 15 constructs inside #if NET11_0_OR_GREATER or a Net11/ folder. Never declare UnionAttribute, IUnion or IsClosedTypeAttribute locally.
Use primary constructors only on non-public classes and structs.

Never assign to a primary-constructor parameter; set MA0143 to error. Never both capture and initialize from one parameter, and never suppress CS9124, CS9107 or CS9113. Read validated parameters through their field. Never enable IDE0290.
Internal records are a sealed record or a readonly record struct with scalar members only. No collection members, and no non-readonly record struct.

Set dotnet_style_prefer_collection_expression = when_types_exactly_match. Never cast or mutate a collection expression typed as IEnumerable, IReadOnlyCollection or IReadOnlyList. Raising IDE0028 and IDE0300-0305 to warning is a SHOULD.

Enum switches have one arm per named member plus a throwing discard; set IDE0072 and IDE0010 to warning. In open-enum struct switches the discard means unknown or failure, backed by a reflection conformance test. List-pattern switches end in a discard.

No hand-written file carries a generated-code marker: no <auto-generated header, no prose 'generated by' header, no *.g.cs, *.generated.cs or *.designer.cs name, no [GeneratedCode], and no committed file under obj/.
The root .editorconfig ends with [*.cs] generated_code = false followed by [**/obj/**.cs] generated_code = true. Never use a [*.g.cs] section.
Mark a type 'partial' only when a source-generator attribute appears in the same file.

conflicts_resolved: generated_code scoping: the idioms researcher's [*.cs] false + [*.g.cs] true pair is replaced by [**/obj/**.cs] true. Measured in F-CL/gc: pair-g fails every xUnit v3/MTP test project with CA1018/CA1852/CA1707 in obj/ entry points; pair-obj builds green and still catches a planted // <auto-generated/> header (CA1305).

CA1062: CS-BUILD-12's repo-wide none is reversed to warning for src. It is the only mechanical check for dotnet/runtime's 'keep validating' rule (NRE vs ArgumentNullException measured). The F-CL ca1062 probe fired exactly on the 2 unguarded public dereferences and was silent on a checked string? and on internal types.
CS-BUILD analyzer-gate claimed CA2264 makes guards on non-nullable parameters redundant. This is wrong: CA2264 fires only on value types, nameof and new expressions. Guards stay.

#nullable directives: the nullability researcher allowed '#nullable disable // reason'; the idioms researcher banned every directive. Decision: ban all directives in hand-written src and tests. The SDK has no unconstrained-generic converter framework, and one grep catches both per-file enable and disable.

IDE0370 location: the nullability researcher put it in .globalconfig. Decision: IDE severities go in .editorconfig with CS-BUILD-14's IDE lines; CA, RS and MA severities stay in .globalconfig. IDE0370 was watched working from .editorconfig.

Async guards: CS-ERR R-EXC-23 said guards throw synchronously, and the nullability researcher proposed a non-async wrapper. Decision: guard on the first line and let the exception fault the Task, with no wrapper, because the surface is async-only. R-EXC-23's wording is corrected.
RespectNullableAnnotations: the nullability researcher wanted it on strict contexts only. CS-JSON-08's single-context decision stands and is not re-decided.

MA0143 vs CS-BUILD-15's two-pack limit: MA0143 rides on the Meziantou reference CS-API-03 already adds (mode None, per-rule line), so no new package. CS-BUILD-15's count check must be updated to three.

CS-PROC-23 ('.NET 11 APIs behind #if NET11_0_OR_GREATER') vs dead code under the SDK 10 pin: no such region may exist until a net11.0 leg builds it (CS-LANG-16). CS-PROC-23 stays the shape rule for later.
field-local diagnostic ID: the docs say CS9272 and SDK 10.0.401 prints CS9273. Checks match both IDs.
IDE0007/IDE0008 'none' lines dropped as no-ops: AnalysisLevel 10.0-all does not raise IDE rules, as the IDE0370 control showed. IDE0290 is kept only as 'never enable'.
Duplicates folded: CS1736 is self-correcting; generated-shape public types fall under CS-API-03/04; contextual-keyword names fold into CS-LANG-11; internal record/collection grep reuses CS-API-04.

rules.rule: Build argv only with ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList. Never use Arguments, the (string,string) constructor or Process.Start(string,string). The RS0030 BannedSymbols file must be wired as AdditionalFiles.
Create the ProcessStartInfo in exactly one seam: UseShellExecute=false, CreateNoWindow=true, an explicit WorkingDirectory, and all three streams redirected.

FileName is only the absolute path the resolver chose once, in this order: explicit option, then override variable, then absolute PATH entries matched by exact name (no cwd, no PATHEXT), then $OCX_HOME. A PATH or home-tier hit must pass a trust check on its directory and its file: POSIX mode bits, or CS-PROC-25 on Windows. Each skipped hit is listed in the NotFound error.
Refuse every .cmd/.bat target, compared case-insensitively, in the resolver and again at the seam.

Catch launch failure only as Win32Exception around Process.Start and map NativeErrorCode (2/3, 0/5/13, 8/193/216, 7/206) to one OcxLaunchException with a failure enum. Never write an unfiltered catch (Exception).

Inherit the environment, then scrub these 7 keys OrdinalIgnoreCase: OCX_PROJECT, OCX_GLOBAL, OCX_QUIET, OCX_NO_VERIFY, OCX_NO_HOOK, OCX_NO_COMPLETIONS, CLICOLOR_FORCE. Set OCX_NO_UPDATE_CHECK and OCX_BINARY_PIN. Mutate only psi.Environment. OCX_OFFLINE, OCX_FROZEN and OCX_NO_CONSENT are deliberately not scrubbed.

Every call, passthrough included, starts with --format json --color never before the subcommand. Never send --quiet. Project handles pass --project <absolute ocx.toml>. Refuse operands that start with '-', and put '--' before exec child argv.
Pass secrets only as stdin bytes or child env vars, never in argv. Types that hold secrets override PrintMembers. Run captured stderr through one redactor.
Drain stdout and stderr with one byte-pump task each, started before stdin is written. Wait with WaitForExitAsync. Ban ReadToEnd*, Begin*ReadLine and the synchronous WaitForExit.
Cap each capture at 16 MiB, discarding past the cap but continuing to read. Stdout overflow fails closed. Passthrough output goes to a caller sink while the engine keeps a 64 KiB stdout head.
Use one static UTF8Encoding(false) on all three streams. Ban Encoding.UTF8, Encoding.Default and per-chunk GetString.
Write stdin as exact bytes to StandardInput.BaseStream from a task started after the pumps, then flush and close. Never use StandardInput.Write*. ocx login stores a CR or BOM verbatim.
After exit, bound the drain with DrainGrace (5 s). On expiry seal the captures and return DrainTimedOut=true. Do not throw and do not kill.
Kill only with Kill(entireProcessTree:true), only while the root is alive, followed by a bounded reap. Never use bare Kill(), taskkill or pkill, and never create a job object.
Use a linked CTS with CancelAfter. A caller cancel throws OperationCanceledException carrying the caller's token. An SDK timeout throws OcxTimeoutException : OcxException. Both kill and reap first.
Validate Timeout once: InfiniteTimeSpan or a value in (0, 24 days]. Call CancelAfter only for finite values.
Install no process-wide handler: no CancelKeyPress, ProcessExit, PosixSignalRegistration or sigaction.
Default grace is 0 everywhere. A POSIX SIGTERM rung is opt-in per call for passthrough only, through one libc kill import. Windows never interrupts.

The engine returns RawResult for every exit and never throws on exit status. rules.rule: Every public async I/O method ends with exactly one `CancellationToken cancellationToken = default`, placed last, with no `params` before it.
Forward the token to every callee. Intentional non-forwarding is written `CancellationToken.None` with a reason comment. Non-public methods take the token without a default.
Never add a token by editing a shipped signature; add an overload.
Public async methods return Task/Task<T>. A ValueTask is awaited exactly once, and a public one needs a benchmark.
Every Task/ValueTask/IAsyncEnumerable method ends in Async, private ones included, and no sync method does (VSTHRD200).

ConfigureAwait(false) on every library await, including await foreach (WithCancellation alone does not count) and await using. No Task.Yield and no ConfigureAwait(true). Tests carry none. Gate: CA2007 + MA0004 scoped to src, plus a Task.Yield ban.
Construct every TaskCompletionSource with RunContinuationsAsynchronously.

Caller cancellation (OCE carrying the caller's token) and SDK timeout (OcxTimeoutException) are distinct outcomes, classified via `when (linked.IsCancellationRequested)` with the caller checked first.
Timeouts cancel the work. No WaitAsync(timeout) or WhenAny(Delay) as the timeout mechanism. WaitAsync over owned shared work is the documented exception.
Put [EnumeratorCancellation] on the token of every async iterator (CS8425 at error).
The creator of a Process, CTS, linked CTS or registration disposes it with using/await using, or transfers it into a handle. No bare Register().
No finalizer, no Dispose(bool) and no GC.SuppressFinalize. Seal the class instead.
The disposal shape follows the role: a stateless client implements neither interface; a resource owner is sealed, dual-disposable and kills the process tree.
No blocking on tasks in library code (.Result, .Wait, GetResult, WaitAll, Thread.Sleep), enforced by RS0030 and VSTHRD002/103 and CA1849.
[ocx] No sync API in v1. A later sync twin is a separate leaf, never sync-over-async.
No async void and no async lambda to a void delegate, including `OnStderrLine = async`, in src, tests, samples and README.
No fire-and-forget and no `_ =` discard of a task. Pump tasks are awaited on every exit path.
Pass an explicit TaskScheduler to StartNew/ContinueWith, and never return a null Task.

The async gate is explicit per-rule severities (24 lines) plus pinned VS.Threading.Analyzers/IDisposableAnalyzers/BannedApi. VSTHRD003 is none. VSTHRD011 stays at its default and is never set to none.

[ocx] CreateAsync runs discovery and the handshake under the caller's token. OcxClient, its handles, the options snapshot and the handshake hold no Lazy, AsyncLazy, SemaphoreSlim, lock, Interlocked or CTS. A failed handshake throws out of the factory and caches nothing.
Never wrap an async factory in Lazy<> or ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd, and never reference the Microsoft.VisualStudio.Threading library (AsyncLazy).
Shared async work never runs under a caller's (or a linked caller) token; it runs under an owned token. Each caller waits with shared.WaitAsync(cancellationToken).

An in-memory single-flight is a lock around one Task<T>? field, reset on IsCompleted && !IsCompletedSuccessfully. No await under the lock, a private readonly object gate, no ??=, no CAS on a task, and no IsFaulted-only reset.

[ocx] Coalesce concurrent EnsureAsync calls only while in flight and cache nothing (ForceYielding first, owned timeout CTS). Correctness comes from atomic install with an overwrite:false loser path, never from a Mutex or lock file.
A SemaphoreSlim is new(n, n). await WaitAsync(ct) is a statement before try, Release() goes in the matching finally, and .Wait() is never used in async code.

[ocx] OcxClient's XML remarks state that it is thread-safe, immutable after CreateAsync (options and environment snapshotted), that the SDK serialises nothing (more than about 4 concurrent ocx.toml mutations can give exit 75 project_locked), and that results are not synchronised. A 64-caller cross-talk test and a reflection immutability test back the remarks.

[ocx] The SDK adds no lock, semaphore or queue around ocx invocations. Exit 75 with project_locked surfaces as OcxCommandException.Detail, and mutating commands are not retried (CS-PROC-22 unchanged).
[ocx] v1's only streaming member is Action<string>? OnStderrLine. No IAsyncEnumerable, IProgress, event or Func<string,Task> in the public API, and Progress<T> is banned in src.
[ocx] Every engine entry starts with `await Task.CompletedTask.ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.ForceYielding)` before Process.Start and before the pumps start.

[ocx] OnStderrLine is invoked inline by the stderr pump with no SDK queue. Calls are sequential within a call and concurrent across calls, and none starts after the Task completes (DrainTimedOut caveat documented). No bounded channel or awaited WriteAsync is allowed in the pump.

[ocx] A faulting OnStderrLine follows CS-OBS-28: capture, keep draining, rethrow after the drain. The child is never killed for it. The call's own failure (OCE, timeout, OcxException) wins. A passthrough Stream sink follows the same contract.
[ocx] The stderr line splitter uses a fixed 64 KiB buffer. Past the cap it discards to the next newline and marks the line truncated. The pump never uses ReadLineAsync, MemoryStream or StringBuilder.

When an IAsyncEnumerable is first added: [Experimental], cold and documented, [EnumeratorCancellation] token last, a finally that cancels, kills the process tree and joins, and an unbounded byte-capped TryWrite buffer.

rules.rule: One public sealed OcxClient with a private constructor and a single static async CreateAsync(options?, ct). Discovery and the handshake happen only there. Command handles are sealed with internal constructors.
No public interface or abstract class mirrors the client or its handles. Tests use a fake ocx executable. If a seam is needed later, add an abstract class in a minor release, never an interface.
Seal every public class, record and exception, gated by MA0053 with MeziantouAnalysisMode=None. Never seal a type that already shipped unsealed.

Input and output types are sealed classes with get/init members and required for mandatory members. Collections are IReadOnly*, with no set, arrays or List<T>. A type with a collection is never a record. CS-API-10 governs inputs and CS-API-17 governs outputs.
No public positional record, except the single-Value open-enum wrapper.
A type with a secret-named member is a class, or a sealed record with a redacting PrintMembers.

Open wire sets are readonly record struct X(string Value) : IOpenEnum<X>, and exit codes are OcxExitCode(int). A C# enum is allowed only for sets the SDK produces. No JsonStringEnumConverter or Enum.Parse on wire data.
A wire union is a public abstract class with an internal constructor, sealed cases and an Unknown case. Never use [JsonPolymorphic] or C# 15 closed/union.
After shipping, only additive changes. Never add or rename parameters, change defaults, seal, add abstract or interface members, or drop a TFM. Extend a method with the Roslyn overload pattern.

On consumer-constructible (input) types, required is fixed at first release. A later mandatory key is a non-required init property with [JsonRequired]. Never put [SetsRequiredMembers] on a public constructor. Output types with an internal constructor are exempt.
PublicApiAnalyzers 5.6.0 with generated Shipped/Unshipped files. The RS0016/17/26/27/36/37 severities go in .globalconfig. Never use require_api_files. Per-TFM delta directories.
Run package validation at pack with a baseline from the second release on, plus AttributesMustMatch and CannotChangeParameterName. Never use ApiCompatVersion or committed generated suppressions.
[Experimental("OCXnnnn", UrlFormat)] per unfrozen report family, starting at 1.0 and never during 0.x. [Obsolete] carries a DiagnosticId. IDs come from one registry.

Derive the bump from both the behaviour-table diff and the API diff. A supersedes block, an edited row or a deleted row is a major (minor at 0.y.z). *REMOVED*, PKV006 or non-experimental suppressions are a major. Added lines or new rows only are a minor.

Release order: version, promote Shipped, then a clean pack and publish only on exit 0, after evicting the cached baseline locally. Then bump OcxBaselineVersion, delete stale supersedes blocks, and add the Baseline twin on the first bump.
No DI dependency in the core package. Any AddOcx ships as a separate package, and none until asked.

Output types live in Models/ as public sealed classes with [JsonConstructor] internal T() {} and public required/init members (required may be added later through the wire-contract gate). No public or parameterized constructor, no non-public setter, no Equals/ToString override, and never a public method parameter. InternalsVisibleTo names only the CS-TEST assemblies. Tests use Assert.Equivalent(strict).

No private/protected [JsonConstructor], no private/protected [JsonInclude] accessor, and no [JsonRequired] on a get-only property. Never suppress SYSLIB1222 or SYSLIB1038 (the .NET 11 relaxations are unusable on the net8 floor).

A UnitTests probe deserializes {} through every public JsonTypeInfo of OcxJsonContext and fails on any exception other than JsonException. It asserts it saw at least, never exactly, the [JsonSerializable] count.
No ModelFactory or builder for output types until a consumer records a need. If one ships, use the Azure two-overload protocol plus a consumer-compile canary.
One abstract OcxException plus exactly five sealed leaves: Command, Decode, Contract, Timeout, Launch. A sixth leaf only with an ADR.
One hand-written 13-row ExitTable with a conformance test against errors.json. Unknown codes stay valid data. No exit literals elsewhere, and never classify by kind, message or stderr.
Passthrough commands return ChildExit. They never use the exit table, never throw on the child's code and never retry. An SDK kill surfaces as cancel or timeout.
One decode seam: it is the only catch of JsonException/NotSupportedException, it rejects a null result, and the message carries a bounded, redacted excerpt. It checks schema_version before binding.
Caller cancel propagates as OperationCanceledException with the caller's token. Only the SDK's own timer becomes OcxTimeoutException. Every wrapping catch filters OperationCanceledException out.
No swallowing catch-alls outside the seam, justified cleanup, or a handler that rethrows.
Exceptions are classes with typed get-only properties. No serialization surface, no Exception.Data, no public parameterless leaf constructor.
Message is a fixed template with no argv, env, stdout or stderr. Excerpts are opt-in, bounded and redacted.
No throw-or-not switches. RunAsync throws and ExecAsync returns. Report-then-fail commands take an explicit accepted-code set.
IsTransient is ExitCode == TempFail (75) only.
Never redeclare InnerException or Message with new, and never let ToString or a member throw.

One behaviour table as data at tests/Ocx.Sdk.FakeCliTests/behavior-table.json, loaded with JsonDocument. It has 19 mandatory rows plus a presence test, and every thrown Ocx*Exception type has a row. Rows are filtered by since, never skipped.

Rows assert catch semantics (base-chain type, catchAs/notCatchAs) and only the listed properties, never Message. Pin null only where it is a promise. The unknown-exit row uses 200. No exact ThrowsAsync, ThrowsAnyAsync<Exception> or Verify snapshots of exceptions.
Behavior/ uses only the public surface. It reaches the fake via ExecutablePath at an apphost copy named ocx/ocx.exe, uses no internals, and bounds every sleeping row to 1000 ms or less.

From the second release, the tests/Ocx.Sdk.FakeCliTests.Baseline twin compiles Behavior/*.cs against PackageReference Ocx.Sdk at exactly $(OcxBaselineVersion), the single property that also feeds PackageValidationBaselineVersion. It uses a non-friend assembly name and has a provenance test.
CI runs check-table-diff.sh against the merge base. A deleted or edited row needs a supersedes block. Stale supersedes blocks are deleted at each baseline bump.
ContractTests links the same table and runs the rows that have contract blocks under OCX_SDK_CONTRACT=1. The props subset omits ErrorKind while the pinned ocx predates the error document.
